newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks record strong gains at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks record strong gains at close.

text.p: Foreign buy orders propelled Argentine stocks back into record territory for the year in brisk trading Wednesday, dealers said.
The blue-chip MerVal index jumped 2.1 percent to close at 688.39, stretching January gains to six percent.

"The festive mood continued today with the New York surge, and we should see carryover gains Wednesday," said Jose Napoli at brokers Ignoto y Napoli, referring to a rally in U.S. stocks and bonds after the release of subdued inflation data.
"Local deals were selective and the choice picks were the telephone stocks, which had cheap valuations," Napoli said.
Telefonica and Telecom both shot up 3.5 percent, while power utilities Central Puerto and Central Costanera rocketed 5.9 and 5.2 percent, respectively.
Investors were also cheered by Tuesday's monthly Treasury bill placement of 250 million pesos in 91-day bills at 6.4 percent and 250 million pesos in 182-day bills at 6.9 percent.

"It was a successful placement with rates below the consensus estimate, and it's a good precedent for the global bond deal," said another trader. Finance Undersecretary Miguel Kiguel set off Monday on an international road show for an imminent $2.0 billion bond issue.
Floor volume swelled to a hefty 38 million pesos in the session against 27 million Monday, while over-the-counter turnover eased to 112 million pesos from 167 million Monday.
The broad market index matched MerVal gains of 2.1 percent, with winners blasting losers 57 to eight and 15 issues closing flat.

No main-tier stocks posted losses and only one, construction stock Polledo, closed flat. Among market gainers foods giant Molinos surged 5.5 percent while agricultural holding company Cresud, a second-line stock, rose 6.8 percent.
